maria_support: Customer (org-8472) reporting sudden 401 invalid_api_key right after creating a new key via the CLI yesterday. They ran `rw keys create --name ci --expires 10/03/2026` and expected it to live until Oct 3, 2026 but calls started 401ing.

devraj_engineer: Can you paste the curl you used (redact key) and the exact 401 response body?

maria_support: curl they used (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` and body: `{"error":{"message":"Invalid API key","type":"invalid_api_key"}}`

devraj_engineer: Pulled audit logs for org-8472 -> key id `sk_live_abc123` created at 2026-03-09T23:50:12Z with expiry set to `2026-03-10T00:00:00Z`. CLI parsed `--expires 10/03/2026` as MM/DD/YYYY (Mar 10) not DD/MM/YYYY (Oct 3). Customer is UK-based and used day-first format.

alex_sre: :thinking_face: ok that explains it. CLI should either require ISO dates or be explicit about locale. Can we add a validation error when ambiguous format is passed? Also need a small docs tweak. @jen_ops can you own a quick patch + changelog note?

jen_ops: I will open a small ticket. Proposed fixes: (1) CLI/SDK accept ISO 8601 only, (2) add helpful error if user passes slash-separated date with ambiguous order, e.g. `Please use YYYY-MM-DD or --expires-days`

devraj_engineer: Workaround for the customer: create a new key with explicit ISO expiry: `rw keys create --name ci --expires 2026-10-03T00:00:00Z` or use `--expires-days 365`. I've generated a replacement key for them and confirmed requests succeed (`200 OK`) in staging.

maria_support: Shared replacement key and workaround with customer. They're OK to rotate and will update CI. Marking as resolved from support side. Please follow up on CLI validation + docs so this doesn't recur. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deployment queued: docs/cli -> 1 patch, cli/validation -> 1 patch (staging build 7632).
